label: Cooldown bands
description: How often an ability can be used: the wait from one use until it can be used again. Band the source's cooldown figure alone; do not add the time the effect lasts. Use real seconds at the game's normal multiplayer speed (StarCraft II: Faster). Where the source gives a span ("8 to 12 seconds", "up to 15 seconds"), band its largest value. For an ability with charges, band the time to regain one charge. Edges are exact, and a value on an edge takes the higher band. An ability whose uses come back only at a resupply point or on respawn is per-life, with or without a figure, however many uses its stock holds (a Red Alert minelayer's five mines, reloaded only at a depot, which are also its limited-ammo resource). So is an action that uses up the unit, such as a self-destruct or a spy that is lost when it enters a building. An ability with no wait has no band: leave cooldown out. That covers instant orders that can be repeated, such as unloading, and mode switches that only take time to finish; say in the summary, in words, how long the switch takes. An ability held back only by another kind of stock, such as one that refills by itself or from income (Company of Heroes munitions, the unit's energy), has no band unless the source also gives a cooldown. A boost's own fuel tank, which only that ability burns and which refills by itself, is its cooldown, not a stock: band the time it takes to refill from empty. An energy pool stays a stock even on a unit with only one ability that spends it (the StarCraft II Medivac's Heal).

terms.label: Spammable
terms.description: Under 5 seconds; several uses in every fight.

terms.label: Short
terms.description: From 5 up to but not including 15 seconds; a couple of uses per fight.

terms.label: Medium
terms.description: From 15 up to but not including 45 seconds; roughly once per fight.

terms.label: Long
terms.description: 45 seconds or more; a few uses per life.

terms.label: Per life
terms.description: Uses that come back only at a resupply point or on respawn, however many the stock holds (often one per life or purchase), or an action that uses up the unit.
